title: Rational purity and twisted pairing for arbitrary Weil isomorphisms
statement:
Fix primes $p\ne\ell$, $a\ge1$, $q=p^a$, $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, an algebraic closure $k$ of $k_0$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ in a fixed algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, and $\Lambda\in\{E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\}$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. For a finite-type $k_0$-scheme $T_0$ put $T=T_0\times_{k_0}k$, $g_T=\operatorname{id}_{T_0}\times\operatorname{Spec}(\operatorname{Frob}_q)$ with geometric Frobenius, and $P_T=Lg_T^*$ [def-weil-frobenius-detailed, def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Use the rational/common-stage bounded constructible categories and Weil pairs $(K,\theta_K:P_TK\xrightarrow{\sim}K)$, whose arrows satisfy $u\theta_K=\theta_LP_T(u)$ [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex]. Let $f_0:X_0\to Y_0$ be a separated finite-type morphism of finite-type $k_0$-schemes, and put $f=f_0\times_{k_0}k:X\to Y$. For the purity assertion assume $X_0,Y_0$ separated and $f$ smooth of pure relative dimension $d\ge0$. Use the canonical rational/common-stage smooth purity map $\gamma_{f,K}:H(K)\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf^!K$ for $H(K)=Lf^*K(d)[2d]$ [def-pur-canonical-rational-purity-realization, thm-pur-rational-and-qbar-purity], transported from [def-pur-smooth-purity-map], with pullback, shift and canonical Tate-line transport [def-weil-frobenius-coefficient-twists]. Write $b_K:P_XH(K)\simeq H(P_YK)$ for that transport and
$$ e_K=\gamma_{f,P_YK}b_K(P_X\gamma_{f,K})^{-1}. $$
Use the constructible exceptional adjunction and its Frobenius structure defined by the right mate of the inverse compact-support exchange [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image, def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]. For every rational Weil isomorphism $\theta_K:P_YK\simeq K$, the displayed $e_K$ is that same mate comparison, and
$$ Rf^!(\theta_K)e_KP_X(\gamma_{f,K})=\gamma_{f,K}H(\theta_K)b_K. $$
Thus purity is a morphism of Weil pairs with the specified exceptional structure. When the exceptional counit has its lifted-adjunction Weil structure, the smooth trace $\operatorname{Tr}^{\mathrm{sm}}_{f,K}=\varepsilon_{f,K}Rf_!(\gamma_{f,K})$ [def-pur-smooth-trace] is equivariant too.

For the pairing assertion let $X_0$ be smooth, separated, geometrically connected and of pure dimension $d$, with structure morphism $a_X:X\to s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, and let $(K,\theta_K)$ have site-perfect underlying bounded constructible complex [def-weil-site-perfect-complex]. Set $K^\vee=R\mathcal Hom_X(K,\Lambda_X)$ and give it the inverse contravariant Weil datum; give $K^\vee(d)$ the canonical twist, with scalar $q^{-d}$. Define the pairing by tensor product, evaluation $K\otimes^LK^\vee(d)\to\Lambda_X(d)$, and the normalized smooth trace for $a_X$. For $x\in H_c^i(X,K)$ and $y\in H^{2d-i}(X,K^\vee(d))$ its degreewise form satisfies
$$ \langle F_{c,K}x,F_{K^\vee(d)}y\rangle_i=\langle x,y\rangle_i. $$
Here ordinary and compact-support Frobenius use their canonical point transports [def-weil-frobenius-cohomology-transport]. Evaluation and biduality have their rational Weil structures, and all equations are identities at $E$ and over a common finite coefficient field for $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$. The assertions allow arbitrary rational $\theta_K$, including multiplication by $\ell$ on a point; no Frobenius-stable integral lattice is required, and no properness of $X_0$ is imposed.

proof.text: First work at $E$. Finite type makes $Y_0$ quasi-compact; separatedness makes it quasi-separated. Nagata gives a compactification over $k_0$; base change preserves its open and proper factors, giving $c$ for the rational mate lemma.

proof.text: For this $c$, rational purity naturality identifies the displayed $e_K$ with the right mate of inverse compact-support exchange, for the specified canonical realization. All separatedness, smoothness and coefficient hypotheses hold.

proof.text: Naturality at $u=\theta_K$ and cancellation give $Rf^!(\theta_K)e_KP_X\gamma_K=Rf^!(\theta_K)\gamma_{P_YK}b_K=\gamma_KH(\theta_K)b_K$. This is the Weil-arrow equation.

proof.text: Put $F=Rf_!$, $G=Rf^!$. The lifted functor sends $\gamma$ to a Weil arrow; the lifted counit obeys $\varepsilon_K\theta_{FG}=\theta_KP_Y\varepsilon_K$. Multiplying these equations makes $\varepsilon_KF(\gamma_K)$ equivariant, also for $a_X$.

proof.text: For the pairing, field $D^b_{ctf}=D^b_c$ and stability (vii) give the domains of Hom, tensor and both direct images. Dualizing the local bounded finite-projective models reverses degrees and preserves site-perfectness; the unit is site-perfect.

proof.text: The Hom lift gives $\theta_{K^\vee}=R\mathcal Hom(\theta_K^{-1},c)h_g$; mate coherence makes evaluation a Weil arrow (the two inverse factors cancel). The inverse-contravariant bidual lemma gives $\delta_K\theta_K=\theta_{K^{\vee\vee}}P_X\delta_K$.

source.place: Sentences 3–4: geometric orientation, trace and smooth pairing; expanded using the rational/common-stage adjunctions

proof.text: Tensor evaluation with the Tate-line identity. The twist definition makes evaluation into $\Lambda_X(d)$ equivariant; its canonical point scalar is $q^{-d}$, and the unit scalar is $1$.

source.place: Sentences 3–4: geometric orientation, trace and smooth pairing; expanded using the rational/common-stage adjunctions

proof.text: Set $L=K^\vee(d)$. The cup is $\operatorname{PF}_{a,K,Ra_*L}$ followed by $Ra_!(1\otimes\varepsilon_L)$. Projection and ordinary counit are Weil arrows; lifted tensor and $Ra_!$ preserve them. Composing with twisted evaluation and the shifted smooth trace gives $B:A\otimes^LD[2d]\to\Lambda_s$ with $A=Ra_!K$, $D=Ra_*L$, a Weil arrow. Point tensor transport identifies its fiber with the stated pairing.

source.place: Sentences 3–4: geometric orientation, trace and smooth pairing; expanded using the rational/common-stage adjunctions

proof.text: Apply point realization to $B$ with $n=2d$: degrees $i,2d-i$ give the required invariant pairing for the canonical point actions. The unit-conjugation formula gives equality of its scalar values.

source.place: Sentences 3–4: geometric orientation, trace and smooth pairing; expanded using the rational/common-stage adjunctions

proof.text: Common-stage descent simultaneously realizes the objects, $\theta^{\pm1}$, comparisons and vectors; the finite-stage equations pass to their classes. For $d=0$, $\theta=\ell$ gives dual $\ell^{-1}$; zero objects give zero. The factors remain $Ra_!$ and $Ra_*$ even when $X_0$ is nonproper.
